A festival. A kite in a tree. Everybody laughing. I saw it in the shard.
A brush. One line on white paper. A teacher laughing. I saw it in the shard.
A card table in a storm. My grandmother's laugh. I saw it in the shard.
A smithy. Every tool on the wall turning to look at a cradle. I saw it in the shard.
...Two of you. One in the room, and one in the glass of my cell. The harbour's bright-line girl. I had hoped.
The lamp in my cell just went out, and I am not afraid. So it is you. The dark watch.
Captain. You are a long way from the wall. ...No. The wall is a long way from us both.
The weight has gone out of my chains. Navigator's star. They told us you had fallen.
You are exactly on time, tide-keeper. You always were. I had stopped counting.
She sings one long note. In the glass of the cell, your reflection learns to stay behind when you go.
She sings one long note. Somewhere in it is a cut you have not made yet, waiting where you will leave it.
She sings one long note. You remember the oldest lesson of the wall: let them strike, and answer.
She sings one long note, and for its whole length everything in the cell weighs exactly what you tell it to.
She sings one long note. You hear it end before it begins, and learn the way back to where you were standing.
You were by the gate. Then by the fire. I never saw you cross. There's a door out in the Ash Dunes that does the same: just a door, no wall. Thought you should know.
You shook my hand from over THERE. I'm choosing to be fine with it. One of my wagons is sunk to the axles out in the Dunes, if those arms are for hire.
You've not taken your hand off that hilt, and you've not drawn it either. There's an old duelling banner out in the Dunes. Nobody here knows whose.
I know a card-player's eyes. Don't sit at my table. ...There's a wanted poster nailed up out in the Dunes with a face a lot like yours.
Every buckle on my harness is pointing at you. The mules don't like it. There's a dead war-machine half buried in the Dunes that's been humming since you arrived.
My shaving mirror's shown me the back of my own head since you walked in. Fix that before you leave.
...Somebody's standing there. Aren't they. I can see the dust not settling. All right. Welcome, whoever you are.
You've stood guard at my gate for an hour, and nobody asked you to. Stay as long as you like, Captain.
My hat's floating. Just the hat. I'd take it as a kindness if you'd let it down.
You answered that before I asked it. Twice. I'll save us both the time and just nod.
(Three people on the wrong side of a locked door. I am good with doors.)
(Raiders, out of arm's reach. They think.)
(Three lives held to ransom. One stroke should cover it.)
(Four hundred creds, and a man who thinks he owns a road. I like these odds.)
(A fortress made of car hoods. Oh, he is going to regret that.)
(A king in a wreck full of chrome and broken glass. Every surface in there is mine.)
(Three hostages. He will not see who took them back.)
(People taken from the road. Then the road needs a guard.)
(A tyrant on a hill of scrap. Heavy things fall hardest.)
(I have seen how this bounty ends. I should go and make sure of it.)
I left it in another room.
Come and take it. From there.
I carry one thing.
I'll see your toll and raise you.
That's a lot of metal you're wearing.
Ask her. She is standing behind you.
Stand aside.
It is heavier than it looks.
You are about to say "get her". Do not.
Everything that crosses the ash, you said. I did not cross it.
You're standing well back. It won't help.
Draw, then.
You're holding a busted flush, Baron. Fold.
Your whole throne is listening to me.
Which of us are you talking to?
Release them. I will not strike first. I will not need to.
Kneel. No - I was not asking you. I was telling the ground.
In four minutes you are on your back, offering me the filters. We could skip to that.
There's a sheet of old window glass standing in the moss just past my camp. Unbroken, after ninety years. I don't look in it.
...Is someone with you? No? Huh. There's a boulder past the pools with a cut clean through it. Older than the war. No idea why I thought of it just now.
There's a rusted standard out past the frozen tree. Blue and white, some harbour crest. Nobody's had the heart to take it down.
Past the overpass there's a ring of stones that don't touch the ground. I threw a rock at one. The rock's still up there.
A Halcyon chronometer came down with the relay crew, just past the second pool. It's still counting. I don't know what to.
You came in without crossing the tree line. I was WATCHING the tree line. Don't do that near the Husks: they notice.
Keep your hands where I can - no, never mind. I can't keep track of where your hands are.
You walk like the stalkers do. Quiet. They'll respect it, right up until they try to eat you.
Bullets work on stalkers. They don't work on Husks. Count your shots.
The relay's all steel. It's been leaning toward Scrapton since yesterday. Toward YOU, I'm guessing.
There is no door big enough for that.
I'm going to need both arms.
Large. Slow. One stroke.
Six won't do it. Good thing I reload.
No metal in it at all. Fine. I brought my own.
Do not look at it. Look at its reflection.
Behind me. All of you.
Everything falls. Even you.
I have watched you die eleven ways. I liked the fourth.
Open the door
The Door You Left
A door, standing by itself in the ash. No wall, no frame, and it is not yours to open.
A door, standing by itself in the ash. No wall. No frame. The handle is warm.
(Mine. I made this, on the way down: a way back, in case I needed one. I left myself a door.)
You open it. On the other side: grass to the horizon, a tent with two flaps, bread on the table. Then it is only ash again.
(Not yet. But it is still there. It will keep.)
Haul it out
The Long Haul
A wagon sunk to its axles in the ash. It would take a team of mules. Or longer arms than yours.
A caravan wagon, sunk to its axles in soft ash. Somebody inside is knocking.
(Four mules could not shift that. Good thing I am not four mules.)
You plant your feet, throw both arms round the wagon from thirty paces off, and lean. It comes out of the ash like a tooth.
(Two drivers and a dog. The dog is the only one who says thank you. I like the dog.)
The Teacher's Mark
A duelling banner, bleached by the ash. One brush-stroke on it, in a hand you cannot read.
A duelling banner, bleached by ninety years of ash. One brush-stroke on it, in the old clan hand.
(My teacher's mark. She was HERE. She came through before me, and left this where I would have to walk past it.)
You kneel. The cord on your sword loosens by itself, the way it only ever did in front of her.
("Still waiting to be told, child?" ...No, teacher. Not any more.)
Read the poster
Wanted: Six
A wanted poster on a dead post. The face means nothing to you.
A wanted poster, nailed to a dead post. The face is yours. The name is not. The reward is enormous.
(Aurelia stamp. Printed BEFORE I fell. Somebody up there knew I was coming, and wanted me found first.)
Tucked behind the poster: a pouch of creds and a note. "If you can read this, Six, you beat them here. Spend it loudly."
(Don't know who you are, friend. But I owe you a drink.)
Wake the core
Old Iron
A war-machine from the old war, buried to the shoulders. Dead iron. It does not stir for you.
A war-machine from the Ashfall, buried to the shoulders. Dead for ninety years. Its core is still faintly humming.
(Old iron. Tired iron. It has been trying to stand up this whole time, and nobody was listening.)
You put your hand on its chest. Forty tonnes of rust sits up, looks at you, and very gently lies back down.
(Rest. You did your part. I will take it from here.)
Look into the glass
The Girl in the Glass
A pane of old window glass, upright in the moss. It shows you nothing but yourself.
A pane of window glass, upright in the moss, unbroken. Your reflection is already looking at you.
(She has been waiting. She got here first. She always gets there first.)
You press your palm to the glass. A palm presses back, and passes something through.
("They are still singing, on the ship. Find the one who can hear them." ...I will tell her.)
Touch the cut
The Cut Not Yet Made
A boulder split by one clean cut, older than the war. It is not your stroke.
A boulder split by a single cut. The faces are smooth as glass. Moss has grown on everything but the edge.
(This is my stroke. But I have not made it yet.)
You draw. The blade arrives, crosses the stone along a line that was already there, and is gone.
(So. I will stand here again some day, coming the other way. Good. That means I live.)
Raise the standard
The Last Company
A rusted harbour standard among empty helmets. It is not your company.
A harbour-guard standard, rust-stiff, planted in the moss beside a ring of empty helmets.
(My company. They came through the tear with me. They held a line here, against whatever grows in this place, with nobody to relieve them.)
You raise the standard. For a moment forty shadows stand to attention behind you.
(Stand down, all of you. The watch is mine now.)
Standing stones that hang a hand-width off the ground. They do not answer to you.
Standing stones that do not stand: they hang a hand-width off the moss, turning slowly, as they have for ninety years.
(Someone told them to stop falling, and never told them they could start again. That is my voice in them. I did this in my sleep, on the way down.)
You open your hand. The stones settle into the earth with a sound like a held breath let go.
(I am sorry. I did not know I had left you waiting.)
Stop the count
One Long Second
A Halcyon chronometer, counting down to something. You cannot make it stop.
A Halcyon chronometer, half sunk in the moss, counting down. The label reads: PULSE TWO.
(Nineteen days, four hours. That is when they fire the Engine again. I knew the number. I did not know that I knew it.)
You cannot stop the count. But you turn your key once, and the last second on the dial becomes very, very long.
(That buys everyone an hour they do not know they have. I intend to use it.)

J: attack - tap for a 4-hit combo. W + J launches, S + J sweeps. Hold S to guard.
Deepline. Under the Pit Arena, where the crowd cannot see: the beast pens.
Psst. Hey. Wolf-man. You're awake. Don't growl, they'll hear.
...Bars. Straw. I do not know this den. I do not know my own name.
They netted you by the sky-pipes. You bit a collector. With LIGHTNING. So the pit-boss calls you Fang.
I'm Pip. I feed the beasts. The latch on your cage is on YOUR side - nobody ever tried it. Walk over with A and D and press E.
The latch is rusted, not locked. It gives.
Oh no. You actually did it. Holt's going to skin me. Here - half my pepper bun. Press Q when you're hurt.
Go EAST, over the feed lofts. Jump with K.
Kennel-Master Holt sells the ones that fight and feeds the ones that don't. Don't be either.
Stray's out of its box. Good. Loose the ferals - I want to see the lightning before I put a price on it.
J: attack - tap for a 4-hit combo. Ferals LEAP: hold S to guard, or dash (L) under them.
A fang on a cord, hung up like a trophy. It is mine. I know it the way I know my own teeth.
(It bites back when I hold it. The storm is in it. The storm was always in it.)
Three ferals. Dead. Do you know what a feral COSTS, stray?
Open the gate.
I'll open YOU. Then I'll sell the pelt to Grist.

Hold S to GUARD his shock-prod. When he flashes white and lunges, DASH (L) through it.
He whistles for ferals - a Chain Bolt (U) hits the whole pack.
You dropped HOLT. Nobody drops Holt. Listen - every beast in the pens is howling!
(Fenn. My name is Fenn. The pack-name can wait. 'Fang' will do down here.)
The stairs go up to the Neon Market. There's an old map-maker there who pays for stories about strays with storms in them.
Deepline. Shaft Nine, the deepest dig in the city. Nobody is supposed to be down here. Nothing is supposed to be down here.
...It's a man. Saints below, there's a MAN in the rock. He's breathing!
...Stone. All around. It was quiet. Why is it loud now? Who... am I?
You tell me, big fella. We cut into a pocket and there you were, asleep in solid granite. The crew's calling you Boulder.
I'm Dov. The foreman's sealed the gallery - says you're 'company property'. Walk with A and D. Come here and press E.
Crake's coming down with his guards to crate you up and sell you topside. I've got kids. I can't fight him.
Take my lunch. Pepper bun, from a stall up in the slums. Press Q when you're hurting.
That rubble is all that's between you and the main gallery. Hit it. Finish the combo: the LAST hit is the heavy one.
Four hits, big fella. J, J, J, J. The last one brings the roof down. In a good way.
That's company property walking around loose. Shaft guards - put it back in its hole.
A loose boulder. A crew of six could not shift it.
(It comes up like it was waiting. The stone is not heavy. The stone is... glad.)
There's my find. Do you know what Aurelia pays for a thing that sleeps in granite?
I am not a thing.
You're whatever the manifest says you are. Crate him.

Hold S to GUARD his hammer. When he LEAPS, get out from under him, then jump the shockwave.
He throws blasting charges - do not stand in the fire.
He's down. Crake is DOWN. Twenty years I've wanted to see that.
(Brakk. That is the name the mountain gave me. 'Boulder' is close enough for now.)
Take the lift up to the Neon Market. The old Cartographer there pays miners for news of anything strange in the deep. That's you.
Deepline. The Vent Stacks: the fan shafts that pull breathable air down from the surface. The city's lungs.
Well. The filter net's caught a lot of things. Never a boy.
...I was falling. I think I have been falling for a long time. I do not remember landing. I do not remember me.
You came down Stack Four on a gust that should've killed you, and it set you down like a cup on a saucer. I've been calling you Drifter.
I'm Nan Coil. I keep the fans turning. Come over here - A and D - and press E. Quietly. The Guild is listening.
The Breath Guild owns the air down here and Big Bellows collects for it. He's heard there's a boy the wind LIKES. He wants to bottle you.
Pepper bun. Eat. Press Q when you're hurt.
The sluice ahead is open - coolant, don't swim. Jump, then dash in mid-air with L. Your scarf blew on ahead of you; it's snagged past the catwalks.
Wind's a patient thing, Drifter. It goes round what it can't go through.
There's the little draught. Boys - hold him down. Gently. I want him breathing.
My scarf, snagged on an intake grille. It is the only thing I own that I am sure is mine.
(It lifts when I touch it. There is no wind in here. ...There is now.)
(Vent-rats. A whole line of them, nose to tail. ...One cut.)
Do you know what a lungful costs down here, boy? I do. I set the price.
The wind isn't yours.
Everything that moves air in Deepline is mine. Now so are you.

Hold S to GUARD his fists. When he flashes white he CHARGES: dash (L) through him and he dazes himself on the wall.
When he leaps, do not be under him.
You've knocked the wind out of Big Bellows. Forty years I've waited to say that sentence.
(Gale. That is what they called after me, when I ran along the ridge. 'Drifter' is not wrong either.)
Ride the service lift up to the Neon Market. The Cartographer there collects people who fall out of the sky. Tell him Nan sent a gust.
Deepline. The Scrapworks, where the Rivet Crew turns the city's junk into things that go bang.
Don't sit up fast. You've got a shackle on and a head full of smoke.
...Bench. Tools. My hands know every one of them. I do not know my own NAME, but I know that is a number-four fuse wrench.
You fell through the roof three nights back. The Crew chained you to a bench to see what you'd build. You built a lock-pick out of a spoon. They call you Fuse.
I'm Sprocket. I'm chained to the NEXT bench. Your shackle pin is loose - walk to it, A and D, and press E.
The pin slides out. You filed it down yourself, apparently, in your sleep.
Ha! Here - pepper bun, they feed us those. Q to eat.
Korr's gunners are in the next bay. Bullets hurt: hold S to guard, or dash through the shot with L.
Korr took your toolkit to the test range, past the slag channel. A weapon artist without her tools is just a girl with opinions.
The bench-girl's loose. Gunners - wing her. Not the hands. I need the hands.
J: attack - tap for a 4-hit combo. Gunners keep their distance: hold S to GUARD the shot, then close in.
My toolkit. Somebody has gone through it and understood none of it.
(Powder, casing, fuse. My hands finish before I have decided to start. ...Oh. Oh, I am GOOD at this.)
You're the best pair of hands that ever fell into my shop, Fuse. Shame about the rest of you.
I don't build for people who chain me to things.
Then you'll build with a gun in your ear.

Hold S to GUARD his shots and cuts. His bombs leave fire on the floor - keep moving.
A grenade (U) bounces once before it blows: aim short.
You blew up KORR. With his own powder. I'm going to be telling this one for years.
(Dyna. It was stencilled inside the toolkit lid. D-Y-N-A. That is me.)
Goods lift's that way - up to the Neon Market. The Cartographer there buys news of anything strange. A girl who fell through a roof and built a bomb counts.
Aurelia. Med-Lab cold storage: Cryo Vault 9. Halcyon keeps what it cannot use yet on ice.
(Cold. But the wrong cold: a dead, humming cold. I cannot feel my hands. I cannot find my name.)
- Subject 52? Blink if you can hear me. Okay. You blinked. I'm choosing to believe you blinked.
I'm Wren. I live in the walls. Somebody just broke out of Sector 7 and the alarms tripped your thaw cycle. You have maybe ten minutes.
Move with A and D. The thaw controls are on the console to your right: press E before the tank re-freezes you.
The tank hisses. Feeling comes back like needles.
There. Grab the med-gel from the dispenser - press Q to use it.
The floor ahead is flooded with liquid nitrogen. Climb the cryo-racks: K jumps, S + K drops through a ledge.
Two guards doing a tank count. They filed your staff under 'stick' and left it with you. Their mistake.
J: attack - tap for a 4-hit combo. Hold S to guard. Guard at the last moment for a PERFECT guard.
An evidence locker. Inside: a falconer's glove, stiff with old frost. My hand knows the shape of it.
(The air goes sharp round my fingers. Feathers. No - ice, shaped like feathers.)
Drones, above you. They hover out of reach - so reach. Hold W and press U.
Subject 52 is ambulatory. That is not on my schedule.
I am leaving.
You are inventory. Inventory does not leave. Drones - bring it back to temperature.

Hold S to GUARD his ice-axe. Dash (L) through the blue orbs.
He calls drones: aim your shards up (W + U) to freeze them out of the air.
You just put the vault custodian on ice. I'd say 'poetic' but I'm busy deleting the footage.
(Isolde. That is what the wind over the eyrie was called... no. That is what I am called.)
The door ahead opens on the admin wing. Three terminals: plug me into each one (E) and I can open Block C. Someone is locked in there who sounds like you.
Aurelia. Med-Lab Sector 4 - or what is left of it. The staff call it the Burn Ward now.
(Smoke. Old smoke. Everything is black except this cell. ...Did I do this? Who was I, that I could do THIS?)
- hello? Subject 44? Please don't set fire to the speaker. I'm a friend. I'm fairly sure I'm a friend.
I'm Wren. You burned this wing down six days ago, so they put you in the one fireproof box they own. Then they collared you.
Sector 7 just had a breakout, so nobody is watching you. Your cell door melted in the fire. Walk to it - A and D - and press E.
The door was never locked. It was welded - by you, from the inside. It breaks like burnt sugar.
Take the med-gel from the wall kit: press Q to use it.
That collar is choking your fire down to nothing. The release console is past the foam vats. Until then: fists. Climb with K.
Hazmat techs, sweeping for hot spots. That's you. You're the hot spot.
That's the console. Hold still, I've never done this bef- oh. It's just a button.
(The collar drops. And everything I was holding back comes UP. It does not hurt. It never hurt ME.)
Subject 44. Collar off. Of course it is.
You should run.
I put you out once, girl. I'll do it again. Suppression team - foam it.

Hold S to GUARD her axe. When she flashes white she CHARGES: dash (L) through and she dazes herself on the wall.
Stay out of the foam: it smothers you.
The Fire Marshal. On fire. I'm not going to say anything. I'm going to think it very loudly.
(Pyra. They wrote 44 on the door. But the forge had a name for me, and it was Pyra.)
Next door is the admin wing. Three terminals: plug me into each (E) and I can open Block C. There's a prisoner in there Halcyon is very careful NOT to burn.
Aurelia. Med-Lab Sub-Level 2: the Core Sump. Halcyon heats half the sector from this room. From one cradle in it.
(Hot. Not burning - the other way. Something is pulling the heat OUT of me. I cannot remember being warm. I cannot remember being anyone.)
- Subject 60? Oh good, you're conscious. That's either very good or about to be very bad.

The coupling lets go. The heat stops leaving. For the first time you can remember, it stays.
Med-gel in the wall kit: press Q to use it.
They've cuffed your output down to a pilot light. The regulator is past the coolant channels. Until then, you hit like a furnace door anyway. J to swing.
Reactor crew. They've noticed the room getting colder.
J: attack - tap for a 4-hit combo. Yours is slow and HEAVY: start it early. Hold S to guard.
That's the regulator. I'm cutting the cuffs in three, two -
(It comes up from somewhere under the floor of me. Rock, made soft. It was never fire. It was the mountain's blood.)
Enforcers, shields up. Don't punch the shield. Put the floor on fire UNDER the shield.
Subject 60 is off the tap. The whole sector's going cold. Do you know what that does to my quarterly numbers?
Find another boiler.
I'll put you back in the cradle myself.

Hold S to GUARD his fists. When he LEAPS, move - then jump the shockwave that runs along the floor.
He throws coolant: it hurts, and it lingers.
Chief Stoker Dren, down in his own sump. The thermostats upstairs are having a breakdown.
(Ashka. The word for the ember you carry from the old fire to light the new one. That is my name.)
The lift ahead opens on the admin wing. Three terminals: plug me into each (E) and I can open Block C. Someone's locked in there - and she's very cold.
Aurelia. Med-Lab detention: the Night Ward. The lights have been off down here for eleven days. On purpose.
(Dark. Good. The dark is the one thing in here that feels like mine. I reach for a name and find only a number on a wristband.)
- Subject 77. I know you're awake: the motion sensors just lost you, and you haven't moved.
I'm Wren. Friend. They keep it dark because the guards kept failing to find you in the light. Then they took your blades, which was smarter.
Sector 7 just went loud and pulled the night shift. Your cell lock is a model I own. Walk to the door - A and D - and press E.
The lock clicks over. You were through the door before the sound finished.
Med-gel, wall kit, press Q. The drains ahead are open: jump, then dash in mid-air with L.
Two Enforcers past that. Riot shields. Don't hit the shield - be BEHIND it. You can walk right through people, apparently. I'm not asking.
There they are. Shields front. So don't be in front.

J: attack - tap for a 4-hit combo. A shield stops everything from the FRONT.
Dash (L) past an Enforcer and cut him from behind. They turn slowly.
An evidence drawer. My kit, tagged and bagged. Twelve stars, two blades, one scarf.
